terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, deponent: most often with accusative and infinitive
evidence: Plaut. Men. 5.2.24: id est, quod suspicābar (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Usually with accusative and infinitive, of guessing that something is so (suspicor eum domī esse). With a person as object it is rare: of suspecting someone Latin says suspectum habēre (see the suspect).

evidence: Cic. Att. 13.10.3: in quem … ulla caderet suspīciō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With long ī, unlike the verb suspiciō, to look up. Suspīciō cadit in aliquem, suspicion falls on someone; in suspīciōnem venīre, to come under suspicion.
Ready to suspect, mistrustful, of a person (Ter. Ad. 4.3.15; Cic. Verr. 2.5.74); of a thing that arouses suspicion, suspectus (see the suspect).
With the dative of the person who suspects: in suspīciōnem alicui venīre.

phrases.latin: aliquandō dormīsse mē sciō, aliquandō suspicor
phrases.english: sometimes I know I’ve slept, sometimes I suspect it
